title: Goulash
subtitle: Hungarian beef and paprika stew
excerpt: Beef slowly braised with a generous quantity of sweet paprika, onions, caraway seeds, and stock until deeply coloured and tender. Hungary's national dish in its most satisfying form.

recipe.sourceNotes: Goulash (gulyás) is Hungary's national dish and one of the few non-French dishes that became widely adopted across European restaurant cooking in the 19th and 20th centuries. The original gulyás was a cattle herder's stew, cooked outdoors in a large iron cauldron called a bogrács. The essential ingredient is good-quality Hungarian sweet paprika: it provides both the distinctive deep red colour and the round, warm flavour. Goulash contains a lot of paprika, more than most recipes suggest. The rule is: fry the paprika with the onions before adding liquid, and never let it burn. German-style versions add caraway seeds; Austrian versions add marjoram. Soured cream on top is served in central European versions.

content.text: Use a generous amount of paprika: three tablespoons is not excessive in a goulash for six. Fry the paprika in the oil with the onions for 1 to 2 minutes before adding any liquid, which blooms the spice and develops its flavour. Do not let it burn or it will become bitter. The beef is not browned before braising in the traditional method: the flavour comes from the paprika and long, slow cooking, not from browning.
Heat the oil in a large casserole over medium heat. Fry the onions for 15 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic, red peppers, and caraway seeds. Cook for 3 minutes.
Remove from the heat. Stir in the paprika and tomato puree. Return to medium heat and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Do not let the paprika burn.

Add the beef, tinned tomatoes, stock, bay leaves, and salt. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook over low heat for 2 hours until the beef is completely tender and the sauce is deep red and thick. Remove the bay leaves. Taste for seasoning. Serve with egg noodles or boiled potatoes and a spoonful of soured cream.
